open_points.subject: OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES
open_points.text: the session cookie's name `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` and its attributes `OWNER_SESSION_COOKIE_ATTRIBUTES`
open_points.question: What exact cookie attributes does this constant contain, including Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Path, Domain, expiry and persistence semantics?
options: Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/; no Domain, Expires or Max-Age
Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; no Domain, Expires or Max-Age
A route-scoped Path or additional attributes fixed by the later owner-interface routes
open_points.default_guess: Use a non-persistent host-only cookie with Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict and Path=/.

open_points.subject: owner-session cookie origin scope
open_points.text: sent only to Registry's own origin
open_points.question: Does “own origin” mean the owner interface's scheme-host-port origin, or only the host/path scope that browser cookie attributes can enforce; if it means the former, what prevents the cookie being sent to the service API on another port of the same host?
options: Require distinct hostnames for the owner interface and service API
Give owner routes a unique path prefix and scope the cookie to that path
Interpret “origin” as host scope and permit the cookie to accompany requests to another Registry port on that host
Replace the cookie mechanism with one that can be scoped to a port
open_points.default_guess: Use a host-only cookie scoped to an owner-interface-only path and require that path not to exist on the service API.

witness.initial: The owner interface and service API are configured on the same IP address with different ports, which A17 permits.
events: The owner signs in through the owner-interface port and receives the session cookie.
The browser requests the same cookie path on the service-API port.
outcomes: Reading “origin” as scheme-host-port requires the browser not to send the cookie to the service-API port.
Reading the available cookie attributes as host/path scoped allows the browser to send the cookie to the service-API port.
witness.observer: The browser, the service API and anyone inspecting the request see the difference.

open_points.subject: sign-out handling of the session cookie
open_points.text: sets and reads the session cookie
open_points.question: When sign-out ends the server-side session, must the owner interface also expire the browser cookie, and if so must the deletion repeat the same Path, Domain and other scoping attributes?
options: Expire the cookie in the sign-out response using the same scope attributes
Leave the now-invalid cookie in the browser until the browser session ends
Expire it on sign-out and on every response that discovers an invalid or expired session
open_points.default_guess: Expire it on sign-out and whenever an invalid session cookie is received, using the same Path and Domain scope.

witness.initial: The browser holds a valid owner-session cookie.
events: The owner signs out and Registry removes the server-side session.
The owner later revisits the owner interface in the same browser session.
outcomes: The sign-out response expires the cookie, so the later request carries none.
The sign-out response leaves the cookie, so the later request carries the ended session identity and is refused before the sign-in page is shown.
witness.observer: The browser and a network trace see whether the ended session identity continues to be sent.
